html:
The Chinchorro were fishing peoples of the Atacama Desert coast, in what is now northern Chile and southern Peru, from about 7000 to 1500 BCE. They made the oldest known artificial mummies in the world, about two thousand years before the Egyptians.

They lived from the sea, taking fish, shellfish and sea lions with hooks, harpoons and nets, in one of the driest deserts on earth.

From about 5000 BCE they began to prepare their dead with great care. They took out the organs, strengthened the skeleton with sticks, packed the body with plant fibre and clay, put the skin back on, and painted it black or, later, red, with a clay mask on the face. They did this for men, women, children and even unborn babies, not only for leaders.

Many mummies have been found around Arica. The sites were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021. The map also shows this people as Chinchorro culture for 2000 BCE.
